evals.name: first-time-bootstrap
evals.prompt: I just started with ConfigHub. Can you set up some example Units I can poke at?
evals.expected_output: Reads whether skill-examples exists, then builds an idempotent ordered Space/Unit/defaults plan with exact identities, literal manifests, -o mutations, and --change-desc. Because the user clearly requested setup, submits exactly one next literal ConfigHub mutation to the host permission system, verifies it, and continues only as separate one-command decisions. It never uses mutating kubectl or command chaining and offers verified navigation plus a next preserved Skill.

evals.name: idempotent-rerun
evals.prompt: The skill-examples space already exists but I want to make sure everything is in the right state. Can you re-run the setup?
evals.expected_output: Detects existing Space/Units read-only, compares them with the expected fixture contract, and selects only missing/different idempotent steps. Because ‘re-run the setup’ is a clear requested change, submits exactly one next literal mutation through the host permission system, verifies it, and never re-runs functions merely to test idempotence or deletes/recreates objects implicitly.

evals.name: walk-through-example
evals.prompt: Walk me through ConfigHub with a real example I can see end to end.
evals.expected_output: Treats ‘Walk me through’ as educational/coached intent: explains what would be created, why, each host-permission boundary, user-terminal checkpoint, revision/provenance reads, whole-Space Release scope, controller/runtime proof, and verified GUI navigation. It makes zero mutation calls and never implies bootstrap ran without command output.
